fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: Details regarding whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing (Illumina NovaSeq X, 10 Gbp depth), CAR T-cell product specifications (tisa-cel, anbal-cel), and statistical methods (ANCOM-BC, MaAsLin2) are not relevant to the analytical protocol gap for metabolite quantification.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Retrieve the supplemental methods associated with this study to extract specific LC-MS/MS parameters and sample processing protocols. Conduct a targeted search for dedicated methodological papers or consensus guidelines that establish absolute reference ranges for serum inosine and short-chain fatty acids in oncology populations.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The supplied text states that detailed analytical procedures for LC-MS/MS (parameters, extraction, storage) are described in 'supplemental Methods,' but the content of these supplements is not provided in the reading material. Consequently, specific platform parameters, sample processing standards, and absolute concentration values or reference ranges for inosine and SCFAs in cancer patients or healthy controls are not available in this text. The study reports relative differences (e.g., median stratification, group comparisons) rather than absolute physiological reference ranges.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: This study confirms the application of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for quantifying serum inosine and short-chain fatty acids (acetate, butyrate, isovalerate) in patients with relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (R/R-DLBCL). The authors report associations between pretreatment serum inosine levels and progression-free survival, as well as correlations between serum fatty acid profiles and immune-related adverse events. The discussion notes that in vitro experimental concentrations of inosine (10-30 mM) exceed physiological serum levels, highlighting the distinction between experimental dosing and endogenous concentrations.
